ai.description: Beddome’s Night Frog (25–35 mm) is brown with a distinct, pale-spotted underside. It features a pointed snout, prominent toe pads, and skin folds along its flanks. It is endemic to the Western Ghats.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus beddomii* is best distinguished by the presence of distinctly enlarged, flattened discs on the tips of its fingers and toes, which are absent in many similar congeners.
ai.habitat: Beddome's Night Frog inhabits evergreen forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 700 and 1,500 meters near rocky streams.
ai.behavior: Beddome's Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky stream banks of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: Beddome's Night Frog breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying 20–30 eggs in terrestrial clutches on rocks or vegetation near streams, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: Beddome's Night Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting evergreen forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Beddome's Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard while perched on rocks or vegetation near fast-flowing forest streams.
